text:
sam: quick spike notes. trying to land direction for SDK iterator surface across py/ts/go. big questions: 1) who owns retries & resume logic? 2) how to version resume tokens? 3) how to support streaming vs paged transports without leaking complexity to users.
maya: tl;dr: keep user-facing API minimal (next()/for await), push transport complexity into adapters, but standardize a tiny resume token envelope so servers + adapters interop.
tom: +1. also we must ensure resume tokens are forward/backwards compatible. a version byte + optional proof HMAC seems sane.
sam: example: token = base64(version|flags|opaque_payload|hint). server can rotate internals as long as version increments. SDKs should treat tokens as opaque except for a 1-byte version extracted by adapter.
maya: about retries: two-layer model proposed:
 - core (sdk): coordinate high-level retry intents (retry window, max attempts, user-visible backoff policy)
 - adapter: implements transport-specific retry mechanics (grpc stream reconnect, http range requests, multipart stream resumption)

this keeps language ergonomics stable.
tom: edge case: if server acknowledges a window but later says resume token invalid, core needs to decide: throw vs attempt alternate resume path. we should define server response flags: `resume_valid: true|false|unknown` and `alt_resume_hint` (optional).
sam: agreed. include header negotiation to advertise capabilities. e.g. `X-RW-Iter-Cap: resume=v2,multiplex=1,alternate-hints=1`
maya: we also discussed idempotency. every fetch should include `X-RW-Req-Id` and adapters may cache last-successful-resume per connection to avoid double-apply on transient reconnect.
tom: language ergonomics: python -> generator/async generator; ts -> AsyncIterable; go -> iterator that returns `(items, resume, err)` or a channel. adapters hide resume token handling.
ops: ops note: resume token rotation => incidents where old tokens rejected cause user-visible gaps. we should add a server-side graceful deprecation window and signal `resume_deprecated_until` timestamp in responses.
sam: proto response sketch (http/json):
```
{
  "items": [...],
  "resume": "base64-v2:...",
  "resume_meta": {
    "version": "v2",
    "cursor_kind": "offset|page|message_id",
    "deprecated_until": 1680000000
  },
  "resume_valid": true,
  "retryable": true
}
```

maya: adapters should log metric `resume_reject_rate` and fire alert if >1% over 5m for any customer.
tom: multiplexing discussion: profitable but risky. if we allow multiplexed streams we need per-cursor flow control headers and per-cursor ack. prefer to ship non-multiplex first and add multiplex as capability flag later.
sam: migration story: v1 SDKs use opaque token no-version. servers respond with `X-RW-Iter-Cap: resume=v1` for compatibility. when server upgrades to v2 it includes both v1 and v2 tokens for a while. adapters should accept either.
maya: quick API sketch (python):
```py
# user code
for item in client.list_things(query):
    process(item)

# internal: client.list_things returns Iterator that wraps adapter
```

tom: tests: add fuzzing for malformed resume tokens, stale tokens, and rapid server-side rotation. also simulate reconnects mid-window.
ops: add runbook: on "resume_deprecated_until" breach, surface user-visible warning and provide link to retry pattern.
devx-bot: RFC draft created: https://r.rw/sdks/iter-surface-v1 (auto) :bookmark_tabs: 
sam: action items: 1) write adapter capability schema + headers (maya) 2) sketch token envelope & HMAC proposal (tom) 3) prototype python generator + http-range adapter (sam) 4) ops runbook + alerts (ops)
maya: i'll open PR for adapter interface with minimal methods: `fetch(window, resume)`, `close()`, `capabilities()` and clear error types: `TransientError`, `ResumeInvalid`, `FatalError`.
tom: i'll add token parsing helpers for go + ts.
sam: ok if no blockers i'll convert this into a short RFC and include example http/json responses + test vectors. :thumbsup:
